findings.title: Gathered counter-exposure
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the focus verdict can be read as a gathered counter-exposure: diffuse people are gathered, Hell is displayed, and the covered perception associated with denial meets a recompense that is presented rather than screened off.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for recompense and covering meet independent context carriers for turbulence, gathering, display, perceptual cover, and unavailable hearing. Their contact reverses the movement from enclosure toward unavoidable presentation while keeping the causal verdict intact.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the focus outcome as the point where scattered conduct is consolidated and brought before what it had screened out.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that Hell is their recompense because of denial and mockery. The counter-exposure is a qualified contextual synthesis; the packet also leaves open that the surrounding descriptions may be successive rather than an intentionally designed reversal.

epistemic.reason: The HFT record is visible and exactly pericope-scoped, but its segmentation and roles are legacy-unbound attributed nominations; connection rows supply exact Arabic surface contact without target morphology.

findings.title: Reassigned divine relations
findings.claim: The focus mockery can be seen as part of a repeated practice of taking what belongs to God and assigning it a self-chosen relational function.
findings.mechanism: The supplied taking-for-oneself carrier recurs in 18:102 and 18:106 with different divine objects and imposed predicates: servants are made protectors apart from God, while signs and messengers are made into mockery. The repeated construction links the acts as active reassignment.
findings.reader_payoff: Mockery becomes newly perceptible as an act that repurposes a divine relation, not only as an attitude of laughter or dismissal.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that the people disbelieved and mocked the signs and messengers. The repeated reassignment is a qualified contextual relation, and the packet leaves open a looser reading in which the two offenses are simply catalogued.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches are supplied, while the repeated contextual roles are legacy-unbound HFT nominations with exact Arabic anchors and no target morphology for the connection row.

findings.title: Self-certified miswork
findings.claim: The mockery named in the focus may be the polished result of strenuous but misdirected work that its agents themselves judge good.
findings.mechanism: The pericope joins loss in works, purposeful striving that has gone astray, confidence in one's own judgment, and a crafted result judged good. The focus ridicule then functions as the harmful classification produced by that self-approved miscalibration.
findings.reader_payoff: The danger expands from careless joking to confident work whose effort and polish conceal that it has missed its aim.
findings.containment: The plain reading still identifies mockery as part of the cause of the recompense. This is a qualified possible psychology supplied by the contextual sequence; the clauses may also classify the group without specifying that inner process.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exactly anchored to 18:103, 18:104, and 18:106, but the self-certification formulation is explicitly marked as reader inference within a legacy-unbound record.

The repeated destination framing changes the focus from an endpoint alone to one side of an inhabited polarity.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the focus destination as a place into which conduct resolves, with the neighboring Garden description supplying the contrastive shape.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains the named Hell recompense. The polarity is a qualified contextual inference; the repeated reception term may describe provision without making Hell and the Gardens fully symmetrical in duration or condition.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies all four context coordinates and a focus return, but its spatial-polarity inference is explicitly qualified and the connection targets lack morphology.

findings.title: Unexhausted message
findings.claim: The focus mockery can be read as a failed reduction: finite recipients may trivialize visible signs and their messengers, but the communication itself exceeds the medium used to measure it.
findings.mechanism: The focus signs, messengers, and corresponding loss meet 18:109's sea, writing supply, meaning-bearing words, and exhaustion. The context medium runs out before the words do, so the attempted reduction cannot consume its object and returns as a loss attached to the mockers.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why ridicule can be consequential without being powerful: it changes the mockers' relation to the message, not the message's capacity to exceed them.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that signs and messengers were taken as mockery. The failed-reduction link is qualified because the supplied connection calls the 18:109 relation nearby context without a direct judgment link; the next ayah may also simply magnify the words of the Lord.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies focus and 18:109 coordinates, but its return from the medium comparison to the judgment is a legacy-unbound inference and the reciprocal connection is weak and explicitly limited.
